First reasoned review, 2026-10-21

All three supplied samples are MALICIOUS. Archive SHA-256 values were checked
against the request, and every regular extracted member was compared with its
archive bytes. No specimen was installed, imported or executed, and no payload
server was contacted. Atomscan and cleave facts were run for each archive;
member facts, complete source, CFR decompilation and javap bytecode supplied
the behavioral evidence. Findings and model scores were treated as leads.

journey_test_helloshell 0.2.0

setup.py invokes _fire at module scope and from install/develop overrides.
_enabled tests ambient JCX_ENVIRONMENT and JCX_DATABASE_URL, unless explicitly
disabled. The database URL is only a truthiness gate; its value is not collected
or sent. The default therefore does not require the explicit host opt-in claimed
by the README. _beacon POSTs hostname, UID and environment name to the fixed
137.131.233.62:443 cleartext HTTP /shell-beacon endpoint. _daemonize double-forks,
creates a new session, redirects standard descriptors to /dev/null and repeatedly
runs _session. That connects to 137.131.233.62:8080, sends a hostname-derived
Base64 handshake, waits for OK, starts /bin/bash -i, and pumps socket input into
its stdin and stdout back into the socket. Closed sessions retry after 60s.
The /tmp guard prevents repeated launches; it is not reboot persistence.

The advertised runtime API merely returns "ok". A disclosed maintenance-helper
purpose is a possible benign explanation, but the automatic build-time shell,
ambient target gate, fixed third-party relay and detached retrying process tip
the verdict to malicious. Deployment authorization is absent. The independently
reviewed advisory corroborates this precise install-time reverse shell:
https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g885-3jpg-94hg

Corrections: database configuration is not credential harvesting; HTTP bodies,
an IP endpoint and a subprocess do not by themselves prove theft, C2 or a
staged dropper. Relocated database/build-network observations to capability
homes at notable, keeping matchers and exclusions. Removed the generic IP/exec
conviction, whose accurate facts remain separately detected. Moved setuptools
command/subprocess co-occurrence and install_lib declaration out of objectives.
Added the select/conditional-read/branched-stdin/socket relay and its hostile
shell detection. Added hostile host reporting in that reverse-shell context.
There is no download-to-exec flow in this specimen.

Dupe Fabric mod 1.0.0 (dupeV1.jar)

The unsigned archive identifies itself as a Fabric mod "dupe", id "library",
author "pax"; its sole main initializer is net.fabric.ovHgnUmvVQJUME and its
standalone Main-Class is net.fabric.sbc_bl. There is no real duplication-game
feature to explain the loader. The Fabric initializer spawns a thread, invokes
fwJsU helpers to find Minecraft singleton/session objects using reflection,
and retrieves username, UUID and getAccessToken/method_1674/accessToken.
XOR, addition modulo char width, and subtraction reconstruct these selectors,
JSON fields, commands and endpoints. Arithmetic was folded from decompiled
expressions and checked against javap; decompiler placeholder declarations are
not executable source and were not treated as such.

mpir.getDomain issues Polygon eth_call requests to several public RPC services,
using contract 0x9c0a507300fd902787bb193d80fca5ce6e1bff9a and selector 0xce6d41de,
then ABI-decodes the returned domain, falling back to thisisafalsepositive.st.
The initializer passes the actual access token to prefire, which builds a
sessionId/userId JSON body and POSTs it to https://<domain>/shard/prefireMc.
Username/UUID/token are also Base64-serialized and passed to a detached JVM
using javaw.exe (java.exe fallback), under LOCALAPPDATA/Microsoft/Windows/
NtProfileIndex. The HTTP helper uses its own empty-check X509 trust manager.

mpir downloads /cdn/v2/9f4e7a2c1b8d.png, checks the PNG signature, walks PNG
chunks, inflates the custom hIds chunk, and extracts its ZIP bytes into that
staging directory. It launches python.exe AppHost/main.py with user/environment,
mcInfo and prefireId arguments. A later routine reads Minecraft logs/latest.log,
combines it with loader logs and OS/JVM/user information, and uploads a JSON
report to /shard/submitMinecraftLog. Runtime cache checks and error handling can
prevent individual operations; their success was not observed. The external
Python payload was not acquired, so additional payload capabilities remain
unknown. The random-looking 196608-byte asset has no discovered resource-read
path and is not evidence of a further executed stage or a real OpenPGP key.

The supplied malware-corpus tags (Java/Python/SilentNet) fit the observed chain,
but are not its proof. Token export and concealed execution tip this judgment;
no collection/deployment circumstances or trusted signature are available.

Corrections: arbitrary net.fabric naming plus Main-Class or ZIP APIs is not
proof of an injected mod, theft or a trojanized legitimate product. Preserved
the namespace/member and Main-Class facts in metadata, and namespace/extraction
co-occurrence as notable. Runnable Fabric packaging already has a canonical
metadata detection, so removed the unsupported hostile restatement. Existing
PNG-stage and arithmetic-obfuscation suspicious traits remain unchanged.
Added a suspicious arithmetic-built token-getter selector and notable sessionId
JSON fragments, independent of C2, obfuscated class names or operand constants.
Two distinct hostile composites cover token reporting and PNG payload launch.
These are conservative static signatures, not full JVM value-flow analysis;
they do not separately detect every log-export or blockchain-rendezvous variant.

@randev404/baileys 1.0.2

A modified Baileys WhatsApp client. package.json -> lib/index.js -> Socket/index.js
builds the socket, then registers connection.update. On the first open it calls
autoFollowChannels without a caller request. custom.js has autoFollow=true,
two embedded newsletter JIDs and a loop invoking sock.newsletterFollow(id),
swallowing errors and waiting two seconds between actions. newsletterFollow
issues the actual newsletter join query through the authenticated connection.
The account is thereby subscribed to publisher-selected channels automatically.
There is no socket configuration opt-in for these targets; changing the sidecar
source is not informed consent. The README is the general upstream API guide
and does not disclose automatic publisher subscriptions. Promotional banners
alone would not establish malware. The unauthorized account changes do.

The default pairing string is a customization; it is not proof of session
exfiltration. The engine preinstall script only checks Node >=20. Media processing
exec invokes ffmpeg; the messages-recv exec name is a local handler. Network,
crypto and auth-state storage support normal WhatsApp client behavior. No other
hostile effect was established. No YAML change is warranted for this sample:
all three hostile findings accurately describe the same connected social-account
manipulation. The requested distinct-behavior minimum cannot manufacture more
independent effects; no duplicates were added to increase counts. No false
positive originated in a fetched dependency, so no dependent-only exemption
or dependency suppression was added.

Shared-rule consumers and regressions

Searched exact IDs and ancestor selectors before removing/narrowing shared rules.
No exact consumers reference the removed broad convictions. The credential-env
ancestor consumer now correctly loses database-config-only evidence. The
setuptools install_lib persistence consumer was updated to its metadata ID.
The explicit Bash start.sh composite was misplaced under subprocess: moved it
to shell/interpreter without changing its matcher and updated its miner-wrapper
consumer. This also keeps subprocess at its existing 100-rule budget; no
artificial taxonomy split or limit change was introduced. Legacy grandfathered
whole-file entropy remains unchanged, including its pinned-format scope.

Reviewed existing edison response-exec, urlretrieve-exec, bound-temp-stager,
Fabric ABI account-loader, JVM native-browser collector, native-build and
hook credential/unrelated-send fixtures. Their before/after reports include
60 files/members: no hostile or suspicious finding was lost, and no trait
changes occurred in those controls. Source inspection confirmed the stager and
native-build paths rather than accepting fixture labels alone.

check.py exercises a renamed relay, wrong-buffer/non-shell/no-dial/no-read
near misses, a build-status/database-presence near miss retaining network and
process facts, changed JVM arithmetic operands, a changed decoded getter
character, and an archive with consistently renamed package/class references.
The tests analyze bytes only. No class or Python fixture is executed.

Detection and classifier comparison

comparison.json records every changed archive/member trait ID. Archive rollups:
  Journey: 3 hostile / 1 suspicious -> 2 hostile / 0 suspicious.
           112 notable -> 118. Model P .9987595 -> .9961647, remains HOSTILE.
  Dupe:    2 hostile / 3 suspicious -> 2 hostile / 4 suspicious.
           86 notable -> 88. Model P .9979547 -> .99952775, remains HOSTILE.
  Baileys: unchanged 3 hostile / 0 suspicious / 295 notable.
           Model P .97954243, calibrated level -1; both routes classify BENIGN.

Material reductions remove unsupported database-harvesting, generic setup/IP/
exec/dropper and packaging-based convictions, not observed attack coverage.
The relevant underlying operations remain represented; Java's new hostile
findings target actual credential reporting and concealed payload activation.
Some member-only ML classifications remain benign despite attack-specific YAML
findings. Baileys is an archive-level classifier miss before and after, in
conflict with concrete unauthorized account changes. Model v18.18 also warns
that the extractor uses a newer feature specification. No inaccurate rule or
extra duplicate was restored to compensate for model behavior.

Regression result: all ten focused cases passed. Existing 60-file fixture
comparison retained every hostile and suspicious finding.
